title: Klybeck edge: from candidate signal to a bounded investigation decision

boundary.statement: This case connects independent SpongeSquad modules through shared claims, gaps and actions. It is an investigation brief, not an engineering recommendation, a design or a permit basis.

roles.calculate: GIS and source modules calculate. This build only reads their published values and checks arithmetic consistency.
roles.constrain: Rules constrain: unknowns stay explicit, restricted evidence stays gated, and the decision cannot advance past requires-investigation.
roles.explain: AI and presentation layers may explain claims and gaps by ID. They must not add values, upgrade evidence states or change the decision.

rules.statement: Unknown never silently becomes zero. Unknown values are {kind: unknown, amount: null}; no numeric zero appears anywhere in the case.
Missing or restricted evidence never becomes safe or suitable. Such claims carry no permitted use and always point to an open gap.
Known and derived claims are listed separately from assumed and modelled ones; assumptions may only explain or screen.
Every claim names its source module, locator, original source, method, validation and at least one limitation.
Every gap names at least one gatekeeper and one next action, and every reference resolves.
The scenario volume is rain falling on an assumed footprint. It is never labelled as retained volume, storage, capacity or performance.
The decision state is requires-investigation. Recommended, approved, suitable, safe or feasible states are rejected.
The generated case is byte-identical for identical inputs: no timestamps, random IDs or unordered output.

evidence_states.known: Published or directly measured (Data Charter: observed)
evidence_states.derived: Deterministically calculated from named observed inputs (Data Charter: derived)
evidence_states.assumed: Introduced only for a declared scenario or stated without verification (Data Charter: assumed)
evidence_states.modelled: Produced by an explicit model or schematic (Data Charter: modelled)
evidence_states.restricted: Exists, but is released only to a legitimate project or purpose by a gatekeeper (Data Charter: unknown + restricted access)
evidence_states.missing: No defensible value exists yet; it must be measured, tested, observed or located (Data Charter: unknown + other access)

extra_permitted_uses.identity: Use only to identify and locate the case; not as evidence about site conditions

gatekeepers.name: Project owner (not yet identified)
gatekeepers.role: Commissions site investigations and owns the next decision. Street X-Ray names this role for the infiltration test; no person or body has been confirmed.

gatekeepers.name: Site scoping workstream
gatekeepers.role: Owns the candidate indicators and must replace placeholders with spatially joined official data.

provenance.locator: areas header comment: replace with spatially joined official data

claims.statement: Klybeck waterfront (Klybeck) is a named candidate in the Basel Site Scoping Tool.
limitations: The coordinates identify a discussion point, not a surveyed site boundary or footprint.

claims.statement: Screening hypothesis: extensive hard surfaces and limited shade may overlap with heat exposure and reduced local rain retention.
limitations: The candidate's 0–1 indicator scores are illustrative placeholders; they are deliberately not carried into this case as values.
The hypothesis must be tested against official climate, land-cover and runoff layers.

claims.statement: Measured canopy cover and site-specific runoff capacity are not available for the candidate.
Who controls the street edge, and whether works are planned there, is not yet known.
No groundwater protection zone intersects the study point.
limitations: A point query: it does not establish that infiltration is permitted, safe or effective at the footprint.

claims.statement: An illustrative 160 m study segment is anchored to the Klybeck candidate point.
An illustrative 2.4 m edge strip frames the test.
The scenario footprint is assumed to be 384 m² (160 m × 2.4 m).
Whether the strip can be excavated without conflicting with buried utilities is unknown and restricted.
Where the kerb inlet leads, and whether street runoff may be connected and overflow safely, is unknown and restricted.
Whether water can infiltrate safely at the footprint is unknown until tested on site.
No field or community observations have been collected for this segment.
Rain gardens and swales that take pavement and road runoff are in progress elsewhere in Basel (e.g. Sevogelstrasse).
limitations: A precedent elsewhere says nothing about utilities, drainage or soil at this footprint.

claims.statement: The scenario assumes a 20 mm rainfall depth.

claims.unit: m³ of rain falling on the assumed footprint
claims.statement: 20 mm of rain falling on the assumed 384 m² footprint amounts to 7.68 m³ of water.

gaps.question: Where does the inlet lead, and where may overflow go?
Who controls the street edge, and are works planned there?
gaps.blocks: Whether anyone can commission or host an investigation on this strip.

gaps.question: Do official layers confirm the heat and runoff overlap?
gaps.blocks: Whether Klybeck should stay ahead of other candidates in the screening.

gaps.question: What does the street visibly do in rain?
gaps.blocks: Whether the drawn surface-flow hypothesis matches visible behaviour on the street.

actions.title: Request an area-limited utility extract and ask operators for depths and clearance
actions.would_establish: Which networks run under the strip and, from operators, at what depth.
actions.cannot_establish: Whether a rain garden is the right measure; only whether excavation is possible.

actions.title: Ask the drainage / GEP owner to confirm inlet, catchment, connection, capacity and overflow route
actions.would_establish: Whether street runoff may be connected and where overflow may safely go.
actions.cannot_establish: Local infiltration capacity or utility conflicts.

actions.title: Commission an on-site infiltration test at the footprint
actions.would_establish: Local permeability and pavement build-up at the tested points.
actions.cannot_establish: Contamination or groundwater clearance without specialist review.

actions.title: Have a qualified specialist review the test, contamination and groundwater clearance
actions.would_establish: Whether infiltration is a credible mechanism at this footprint.

actions.title: Identify who controls the street edge and whether works are planned
actions.would_establish: Who can host or commission an investigation, and whether planned works change the timing.

actions.title: Replace placeholder indicators with spatially joined official climate, land-cover and runoff layers
actions.would_establish: Whether the heat and runoff overlap holds in official data at area scale.

actions.title: Run a Rain Walk along the segment, ideally during rain, and review every clue
actions.would_establish: Reviewed, time-stamped visual clues: inlets, ponding, tree pits, sealed surfaces, obstructions.
actions.cannot_establish: Pipe connections, infiltration rates, utility depths or any hydraulic parameter.

actions.title: Agree who commissions the utility, drainage and infiltration checks for the 160 m study segment
actions.would_establish: Whether the investigation proceeds, is paused, or the candidate is dropped.
actions.cannot_establish: Whether a rain garden should be built.

observation_plan.boundary: Rain Walk clues are visual, time-stamped and reviewed. They point gatekeepers to what to check; they never confirm assets, connections or clearance.

scenario.label: Rain falling on the assumed footprint during a 20 mm event

may_explain: How runoff can be routed from a sealed street into a planted strip.
Why a connected rain garden behaves differently from an isolated one.
That stored, infiltrated and overflow water are separate quantities.
must_not_be_used_for: Engineering validation of any Klybeck intervention.
Retained volume, flood reduction or design performance at Klybeck.
Soil, drainage or utility facts; Street Lab uses a synthetic street and illustrative parameters.

stages.title: Candidate signal
stages.question: Why is this place worth a closer look?
can_show: A named candidate and a screening hypothesis worth testing.
cannot_show: The severity of heat or runoff; the candidate scores are placeholders.

stages.title: Evidence classification
stages.question: What is known, derived, assumed or modelled?
can_show: Open records give context around the study point; the segment, strip and flow line are labelled as assumptions or hypotheses.
cannot_show: Conditions inside the footprint or under the street.

stages.title: Evidence gate
stages.question: What stops this becoming a recommendation, and who can unlock it?
can_show: Each decisive unknown, its access state, its gatekeeper and the next action.
cannot_show: The answer to any gate; none is available in open data.

stages.title: Field-observation plan
stages.question: What could people on the street establish, and what not?
can_show: Which visible clues to look for and which gap each one informs.
cannot_show: Any completed observation; none has been collected for this segment.

stages.title: Intervention candidate
stages.question: Which measure is being investigated?
can_show: Why a kerbside rain garden is the concept under investigation and that Basel has comparable work in progress.
cannot_show: That the concept is buildable, permitted or effective at this footprint.

stages.title: Illustrative scenario
stages.question: What does the scenario arithmetic say, and what does it not say?
can_show: The scale of rain falling on the assumed footprint in one 20 mm event.
How a rain garden works in principle (Street Lab, synthetic street).
cannot_show: Retained volume, storage, infiltration, flood reduction or design performance.
Anything about Klybeck's soil, drainage or utilities.

stages.title: Bounded decision and next actions
stages.question: What may be decided now?
can_show: Only whether to commission the investigation.
cannot_show: Whether to build, fund or approve a rain garden.

decision.question: Should the Klybeck edge proceed to a bounded investigation of a kerbside rain garden?
decision.bounded_next_decision: Agree who commissions the utility extract, drainage confirmation and infiltration test for the 160 m study segment, and run one reviewed Rain Walk. Nothing is built or recommended at this step.
reopen_when: Utility clearance is confirmed by the cadastral authority and network operators.
The drainage / GEP owner confirms connection and a safe overflow route.
An on-site infiltration test has been reviewed by a qualified specialist.
